quotes.text: Microsoft says it plainly in its own guidance you can't govern what you can't see, and you can't secure what you don't understand.

quotes.text: Agent three sixty five is everything that comes after. It's where an agent gets approved, watched, governed, and eventually retired, which makes it more like a front desk than a workshop.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: The most common one is blocking agents before you have a registry, which is like firing people before you know who works for you.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: The fix is unglamorous and effective. Turn the registry on. Let it fill up and only then start making decisions.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

takeaways: Agent 365 does not build agents; it is the control room in the Microsoft 365 admin center where agents built in Copilot Studio, Agent Builder, SharePoint or Foundry get approved, watched, governed and retired.

The agent registry is the heart of the setup: one list of every agent, with counts for total, ownerless and unmanaged agents, and duplicate rows that are lifecycle records by design rather than inventory errors.

Turn the registry on before blocking anything, deal with ownerless agents early, and remember that delete opens a recovery window, some views need a higher-tier license and not every agent appears automatically.
hook: AI agents are easy to build and easy to forget, so they quietly pile up across your company with unclear owners and access to your data. This Simply Explained episode is for IT admins and curious beginners who want to understand Microsoft Agent 365, the control room for agents inside the Microsoft 365 admin center. You will learn how the registry, admin actions, dashboards and security templates help you see, govern and secure every agent, and where the tool honestly falls short.
